Volley spells are now much more sustainable as a primary source of damage.
Multiple wizards can now play more easily together, as they have their own individual stacks for Reclaim Magic using the new Spark of Magic system described below.
Seal of Magic
While Seal of Magic is active, your Evocation spells still activate Mark of Magic, and your harmful spells now also leave Sparks of Magic on your target.
Mark of Magic

Mark of Magic works as before and is shared by everyone. It increases all Spell Damage the target takes by 2% per stack, up to five stacks, for 1 minute. Reclaim Magic no longer consumes it, so the damage bonus stays up while your group keeps casting.
Spark of Magic

Spark of Magic is new and belongs to the Wizard who left it. Your spells leave more Sparks the more Mana they cost, and Volleys leave the most. Sparks last 1 minute, lower the target's Maximum Mana slightly, and can't be dispelled.
Reclaim Magic
Reclaim Magic now consumes your own Sparks and returns Mana based on how many you had. It no longer has a cooldown, and grants your party Arcane Acceleration if you don't already have it.

Reclaim Magic can't use another Wizard's Sparks, and another Wizard can't use yours. With more than one Wizard in the group, every Wizard can build and reclaim on the same target without taking stacks from each other.
Arcane Volley and Fire Volley

Arcane Volley and Fire Volley now hit five times at every rank, and their damage per hit is about the same as before. Reclaiming after a full Volley returns more Mana than it cost, so alternating Volley and Reclaim Magic lets you keep casting while slowly regaining Mana.

Clerics have two new spells at level 4, Blessing of Smiting and Hymn of Smiting. These buffs allow the cleric to sanctify the weapons of their group, causing them to occasionally channel holy power into their strikes.

Blessing of Smiting blesses a single ally for 35 minutes. While it's active, their melee and ranged attacks have a chance to strike with Sanctified Weapon, dealing Holy damage to their target. Hymn of Smiting grants the same blessing to your whole group with one cast.
Sanctified Weapon grows stronger as the blessed ally gains levels. The two blessings don't stack with each other, so use whichever fits the moment.

We've reworked how spell and ability scrolls are priced so that every class spends the same amount to learn its full kit.

The old prices were set per level, so a scroll cost about the same no matter who bought it. That sounds fair until you count the scrolls. A wizard has far more abilities to learn than a monk, so a wizard ended up paying roughly four times as much to buy everything. We couldn't find a good reason for that - A wizard isn't more powerful than a monk, doesn't need less gear, and doesn't earn more money along the way.

Now each 5-level range has a set total cost that's the same for every class. For levels 1-5, buying all of your scrolls costs 4sp 5cp, whether that's 6 scrolls or 24. If your class has lots of scrolls in a range, each one is cheaper. If it has only a few, each one costs more, but everyone spends the same total.
Within a range, earlier scrolls cost less than later ones, so your level 1 scrolls are cheaper than your level 5 scrolls.
A few scrolls are shared between classes, like Gate. Those have one price for everyone, set low enough to fit every class that uses them.

This does create some eye-catching prices at high level, where some melee classes only get one or two new abilities in a range. We have built the game with the expectation that all classes should be competitive and useful with their full kit, so pricing those to require equal spend feels like a sensible choice.

Buff Durations

Goal - We'd like to find a good balance between class interdependence, and social play for the buffs you can cast on others, while making the process of buffing and rebuffing a bit cheaper and faster.
During the beta period, many buffs were set to a one hour duration to make it easier to test and to get benefit from social buffing.
While we want players to buff outside of their group as a form of social cooperation, the hour-long buffs are reducing the appeal of bringing buffing classes into groups.
Here are the changes we made in this update:
We've reduced mana hour-long buff durations to be 35 minutes instead.
We've also adjusted mana costs to be cheaper in most cases.
Additionally, we've shortened the cast times on many of these buffs to be a bit quicker.
Most self-only and pet buffs were not reduced to a shorter duration as they do not affect class interaction goals.
We've added some group versions of common buffs in recent class updates, and will consider adding more in the upcoming class updates.

While we understand that this change will not please everyone, we are committed to making a game with strong social connection required for success and also providing a pace of play that includes some amount of intentional downtime that leads to more social play.
Buffs and rebuffing are a natural resting point, where mana-driven DPS classes can pause and mediate, the group can chat, and take a quick afk if needed.
Single-Target Healing Update
We’ve adjusted both the healing amounts and mana costs for most single‑target healing spells. Several factors led to this change:

Wisdom scaling overshot expectations. A previous update added a large bonus to healing based on Wisdom. This was a positive change that rewards you for gearing up, but our baseline tuning didn’t account for how large that bonus would become. As a result, heal amounts and mana costs drifted out of alignment.
Healing inflation emerged. Many players reported that heals were simply too large relative to actual player health, making incoming damage feel trivial.

Mana efficiency became too high. With the Wisdom bonus, most heals, especially heal‑over‑time and delayed heals, became more mana‑efficient than intended. This reduced the sense of danger and made mana management less meaningful.

HoTs and delayed heals were under‑costed. These spells should be somewhat more efficient because they don’t deliver full healing immediately, but they were providing too much value for their cost. While they have different mechanics than a normal heal, they are all valuable tools for healing in different situations, and didn't need a big mana efficiency bonus to be valuable.
Why this matters:

Healing and mana management are central to group pacing and social play. Healers should feel rewarded for managing their mana well, and groups should benefit from playing smart to reduce unnecessary healing. Occasional pauses for healer mana:
let casters catch up on regen,
create natural social moments,
and give players brief breaks without disrupting the group.

We’ve consistently aimed for a somewhat slower, more deliberate pace than modern MMOs - something that makes dungeon camping feel dangerous without becoming non-stop action with no time to chat or eat that sandwich.
What Changed
Healing amounts were reduced to more reasonable values.
Mana costs were adjusted to match the new healing numbers.
Single‑target heals were re‑evaluated for consistency and value.
In some cases, mana costs decreased while efficiency stayed the same or improved.
In others, especially HoTs and delayed heals, heal amounts and efficiency were reduced because they were previously over‑performing.
What Happens Next

As always, we’ll monitor player feedback and beta server data to see how these changes feel in real gameplay. We’ll continue refining healing and mana balance to support the pacing and group dynamics we’re targeting.

Consume & Consuming Pact-
Added an alternative version of Consume: "Consuming Pact"
This style of consuming aims to satisfy the players who want to use the ability more often, and are willing to embrace some danger for mana return, with more control over how they use it.
Here's how it works:
1 second cast, with an 8 second recast
A single rank that scales up as you level
Takes some health and returns some mana when cast
Applies a 2 minute debuff that reduces healing on the Shaman by a substantial amount.

You cannot use the normal Consume spells and Consuming Pact while the debuff is up. You can swap freely between them depending on your situation, but need to wait two minutes before using the other style.
Why does it work this way?
Shaman healing is still quite mana efficient, and both Consume and Consuming Pact give a lot of mana compared to other mana regeneration sources available to other classes.
The downside for Consume was intended to be "you get a lot of mana regen, but it's risky because your health is low for awhile."
Unfortunately, pre-update Shaman healing was strong enough that you could gain a lot of mana with Consume while staying at full health easily.

We feel Shaman healing is in a good place after this update and did not want to reduce the efficiency any further, so adding a debuff that reduces healing is a good way to balance that sense of danger with great mana return.

If Consuming Pact feels too risky, then Consume is still available. With the healing balance pass in this update, we were able to reduce the cooldown for Consume ranks 2-4 to 40 seconds, so you can use it a bit more often.

In testing we found that many safer situations allowed for Shamans to use Consuming Pact without much worry, as their tank was managing the active monsters, and the Shaman was in little danger of getting hit. In other situations, especially in dangerous dungeons, using Consume felt more reasonable as it did not have the healing reduction.
Please give this a try and we'll look forward to your feedback after you've had some time to play with it.

Reclaim Magic

AoE reclaim was causing issues in PvP and made it challenging to use in many areas. With some additional concerns reported from community feedback, we're going to return this to being a single-target spell.

After reviewing player feedback and play data, it was clear Reclaim Magic had some concerns. It was challenging to coordinate in multi-wizard groups, and limited options to feel effective using damage spells other than volley.

Reclaim Magic now has a 30 second cooldown, so you can use it two times each minute. It works the same way, in that it reclaims Marks of Magic from a target NPC and gives mana back for each stack that is consumed. For wizards using glyphs, there will be a 30 second 'Reclaim Magic' buff that appears so you have clear feedback on when your cooldown is completed.

The 30 second cooldown should make it easier coordinate in multi-wizard groups so more than one wizard can stack Marks quickly, and can take turns reclaiming for mana. This also opens up options to use other spells than volley to stack up Marks while waiting for your cooldown.
Volley spells are still valuable for stacking Marks quickly in order to get the damage bonus, but it now feels like this is not the overwhelmingly best choice.
Mana return scales from 5 to 25 mana per Mark consumed, based on the caster's level. Reclaiming twice per minute will give as much as 250 mana back.
Please keep in mind that while you're casting you also benefit from standing mana regeneration, the mana regeneration from Sorcerous Mind, and that Arcane Invocation is available every five minutes.
It's important for Wizards to have mana to play effectively, and it's also true that Wizards have many stacking ways to speed up mana regeneration.
Please spend some time playing with this change and share your experience with us.
Quad-kiting

Quad-kiting should be an effective way to play, but should also come with some risks, require skillful play and good gear to be effective, and take a reasonable amount of time to kill four monsters. Quad-kiting should also be most effective on lower blues - not necessarily light blue, but probably on the low end of dark blue.

We want to support quad-kiting as a mechanic, but in the past it has been faster and easier than it should be. We don't want to make it unachievable, but we do intend to make it more challenging than it was pre-update.

If you find you're having trouble quad-kiting solo at your level and gear quality, consider grouping up with another person. Another wizard or Druid can quad-kite also. Several classes could toss DoTs on your targets or otherwise contribute damage. Consider getting some buffs or other assistance. At many levels, solo quad-kiting is possible - but it's even more reliable in duos and small groups if you're having difficulty.
With the change to Reclaim Magic, we've lowered the cost of the Burst spells slightly to offset the decrease in mana regeneration from Reclaim Magic.

We've tested quad-kiting at a variety of levels and found it is still possible and reasonable to do with the intellect available from common quality gear and jewelcrafted jewelry for many level ranges.
If you're finding it challenging at your level while wearing reasonable gear and using good techniques to be mana efficient, we'll look forward to your feedback.

Scaling PvP Level Ranges
Based on 'brackets', and who can attack whom will always use the lower level target's bracket.
1-9 (+/- 2 levels)
PvP FFA Flagging
When performing a beneficial action on a PvP target outside their level range, a player will be flagged "PvPFFA" status.
This lets them become freely attackable by anyone of any level for the duration of the status.
Note: a FFA player still can only attack within their level range, leaving FFA players particularly vulnerable.
PvP Opt In Flagging

A player may choose to perform harmful actions on a (higher) level player outside of their level range. Doing so will flag the player as "PvPOptIn" status which makes them freely attackable to anyone higher level than them for the duration.
PvP Player Name Colors
Overrides PvP player names based on if a player can or cannot be attacked.
Red Name (or pink of roleplay) -> Player is within level range, or can otherwise be attacked via their PvPFFA or PvPOptIn status.
Orange Name -> Player is outside of level range, but higher level, and you can choose to "Opt In" and attack them. This would result in a PvPOptIn status.
Blue Name -> Player is not within range and is otherwise not able to be attacked.
PvP Consider Text/Colors
Adjusts consider text for PvP flagged players.
White Con -> Within level range
Red Con -> Out of level range, higher level
Green Con -> Out of level range, lower level
Also will indicate if a player is within a PvPFFA or PvPOptIn status, as well as display additional verbiage if they are over 10 levels in either direction.

Buffs from player abilities now show a description on their tooltip

Major change in UI Scale - The design of the UI scale has been made for 2560x1440 since I (encrypt) have taken over. You may notice that your UI looks smaller now (or bigger if you are in 4k), this is expected - the UI will now scale properly with the window size of the client. Please adjust your UI scale to your liking
The sale panel at the bottom of a merchant window will now properly gray out the buy/sell button if the selected item is not wanted by the merchant
The merchant panel should now behave correctly when changing the pivot on this window
You can now right click player names in chat to access a context menu with the options to send a tell, invite, consent, or ignore
A confirmation will pop up if you select ignore to prevent misclicks
Spells can now be cast uninterrupted while your spellbook is open, even as your character stands and the book closes

Tell windows will now function as classic chat mode only, so if you use `/ooc` or another channel, it will properly route to it. All other messages in that window will go directly to the player if no channel is specified
`/consent group` & `/deny group` have been added to allow or remove all players in your group from dragging your corpse

New command to ignore players by account to prevent harassment - if you use `/ignore playername account` it will ignore all characters on that account. Additionally, `/ignore list` now shows who is on your ignore list
A profanity filter has been added to commands, with a default of "on". Use `/filter on | off` to toggle it
A notification has been added when you gain a cantrip slot. Cantrips allow you to assign a memorized spell to not be lost on death by clicking the number assigned to the spell on the ability bar
Archers now have access to the Parry skill
Rogues now have a chance to critically hit when using Throw starting at level 21
Classes that should not have access to Tracking can no longer train it only to find it didn't work for them
Paladins can now critically hit undead with auto attacks as well as their Might and Martial abilities starting at level 21 via the Righteous trait
Fighters can now critically hit with their Might and Martial abilities (in addition to their existing auto attacks) starting at level 21 via the Fierce trait
The Paladin ability Restorative Smite has been redesigned
It can no longer double hit while the target is under a Slam stun
Instead of requiring an execution for the group heal, it will consume one charge of Fulfillment (the Supplication line proc) to heal for the same amount as previously
The Shadowknight ability Shadow Strike has been redesigned
It can no longer double hit while the target is under a Slam stun
It will now reset the duration of any of the Shadows line (DoT snare) on the target
The Inquisitor ability Purifying Blow will no longer double hit while the target is under a Slam stun
Its dispel proc remains unchanged
The Spellblade ability Infuse Weapon: Spark now properly grants its buff
The experience required to level Beastmaster pets has been reduced, allowing them to catch up more easily
Beastmaster pets will no longer equip weapons traded to them
Beastmaster pets now have their damage scale more smoothly each level instead of increasing at set points
This further differentiates them from their summoned counterparts and is a small damage increase at most levels
Call Companion no longer has a resist check
Wizards no longer have access to the Dual Wield skill. It has been replaced with a specialized version of Dual Wield that allows them to equip a staff in the offhand
Rogues now have access to the Distract ability
Feign Death should now result in fewer trains, and be easier to split packs with
New ability that strips all buffs cast by someone above or below a defined level
Riding Supplies vendors now sell a basic pack rigging for attaching to donkeys
